Keep imported material, placement, compaction, and trucking assumptions clear in the estimate.

definition_en: The work required to prepare the supporting surface beneath a concrete slab, which may include trimming subgrade, granular material, compaction, leveling, and other specified under-slab layers.
explanation_ru: Подготовка основания под бетонную плиту. Scope может включать trimming subgrade, gravel/base material, compaction и доведение отметки перед concrete work. Точный состав нужно брать из details/specifications.
translation_vi: chuẩn bị nền dưới sàn bê tông
example_en: Carry slab preparation separately from the structural concrete if it is a distinct trade scope.
scenario: Before concrete placement, the entire floor area needs a uniform compacted support surface at the required level.
visual: Slab cross-section showing concrete above a prepared granular layer and compacted subgrade.
common_mistakes: Slab preparation scope varies widely between projects and trade packages.
Do not assume vapour barrier, insulation, mud slab, or granular thickness unless shown.

definition_en: A broad, relatively thin reinforced or unreinforced concrete structural or ground-supported element forming a floor, roof, parking deck, or working surface.
explanation_ru: Бетонная плита. В контексте встречи важны existing parkade slabs и новые slabs, внутри/под которыми идут below-grade services. Плита может быть slab-on-grade или suspended — это разные конструкции.
example_en: Coordinate the below-grade plumbing before the concrete slab is poured.
scenario: A large horizontal concrete element forms the floor or parking deck and covers the underground work below it.
visual: Section through a horizontal concrete floor with reinforcement and utility piping below.
common_mistakes: A concrete slab is not automatically slab-on-grade; some slabs are suspended.
Check thickness, reinforcement, support condition, and construction joints in the structural drawings.

definition_en: A numerical way to express the steepness of a slope, commonly as horizontal distance to vertical distance (H:V), such as 1.5H:1V.
explanation_ru: Отношение уклона — запись крутизны откоса, обычно Horizontal:Vertical. Например, 1.5H:1V означает 1.5 единицы по горизонтали на 1 по вертикали. Всегда проверяй, в каком порядке записан ratio.
example_en: Confirm the slope ratio shown in the geotechnical or structural note before calculating the excavation footprint.
scenario: A drawing note gives two numbers separated by a colon to define how far a line moves horizontally for each unit of vertical change.
visual: Right triangle showing horizontal run, vertical rise, and an H:V label on the inclined face.
common_mistakes: Do not assume every ratio is written H:V; read the drawing note.
A project-specific influence-line ratio is not automatically the same as a safe excavation slope.

definition_en: The vertical height of a point relative to a stated datum or benchmark, used to define grades, inverts, floors, excavation bottoms, and structural levels.
explanation_ru: Отметка высоты точки относительно принятого datum/benchmark. В takeoff разница между existing, slab, invert и bottom-of-excavation elevations превращается в depth.
example_en: Use the correct elevation from the architectural, structural, and civil drawings when calculating excavation depth.
scenario: A plan or section gives a numeric vertical level that must be compared with another level to determine depth or height.
visual: Profile with a benchmark line and several points labelled at different vertical levels.
common_mistakes: Elevation is a vertical level, not the same as depth.
Confirm the drawing datum and units before comparing elevations from different disciplines.

definition_en: A layout in which adjacent floors, slabs, parking decks, or foundation areas occur at different elevations rather than one continuous level.
explanation_ru: Разноуровневая схема: соседние части здания или parkade находятся на разных отметках. Для excavation это важно, потому что один footing может начинаться от P2, а другой от P3, и глубина будет разной.
example_en: Treat the split level carefully because the same footing type may have different excavation depths on each side.
scenario: Two adjacent floor areas are offset vertically and connected by a step or ramp rather than forming one flat plane.
visual: Building section with two adjacent slabs at different elevations connected by a step.
common_mistakes: Do not use one average level across a split-level structure unless the estimating method explicitly allows it.
Check which level each footing or service belongs to.

definition_en: The handling and legal removal of excavated soil, rock, debris, or unsuitable material from the site to an approved reuse, recycling, or disposal location.
explanation_ru: Вывоз и размещение excavated material за пределами площадки. В estimate это отдельный cost driver: loading, trucking, dump/tipping fees, material classification и destination могут существенно менять цену.
translation_vi: vận chuyển đất đào đi đổ
example_en: Separate excavated material disposal from excavation and trucking when the estimate tracks those costs individually.
scenario: The site has more excavated soil than can be reused, so excess material must be hauled to an approved destination.
visual: Excavator loading a truck with arrows from the site to an off-site disposal facility.
common_mistakes: Excavation, trucking, and disposal fees may be separate cost components.
Material acceptance and disposal requirements depend on classification and destination.

definition_en: The use and pricing of haul trucks to move excavated material, aggregate, fill, demolition debris, or other construction materials between the site and external locations.
explanation_ru: Автоперевозка материалов самосвалами/haul trucks. Для earthworks estimator важно отделять truck time/loads от excavation, material supply и dump fees и учитывать haul distance, cycle time и loading constraints.
translation_vi: xe ben vận chuyển vật liệu
example_en: Price trucking separately when excavated soil must be hauled off site and imported aggregate must be delivered.
scenario: Material must move between the project and an external source or disposal site, requiring repeated truck cycles.
visual: Haul truck traveling between an excavation site and an external material or disposal location.
common_mistakes: Trucking cost is not the same as disposal or material supply cost.
Production depends on haul distance, queueing, load time, dump time, traffic, and truck capacity.

definition_en: An estimating error in which the same quantity or scope is measured or priced more than once because overlapping items are not reconciled.
explanation_ru: Двойной учёт. В этой встрече пример — trench проходит через footing excavation: если footing volume уже включает этот объём, нельзя снова полностью посчитать его как trench excavation.
example_en: Check trench and footing overlaps to prevent double counting in the detailed excavation takeoff.
scenario: Two takeoff items overlap physically, and adding both full quantities would charge the same volume twice.
visual: Plan view with two overlapping takeoff shapes and the overlap highlighted once.
common_mistakes: Do not remove legitimate separate work just because two scopes occupy the same area.
Use clear takeoff boundaries and reconciliation notes for overlaps.

definition_en: A vertical structural member, commonly steel H-pile, installed at intervals to support an excavation shoring wall, with lagging spanning between adjacent piles.
explanation_ru: Вертикальная несущая стойка шоринга, часто стальная H-pile. Между соседними soldier piles устанавливают lagging; сами стойки могут удерживаться tiebacks, walers или внутренними распорками.
translation_vi: cọc thép giữ thành hố đào
example_en: Install each soldier pile before the excavation proceeds to the next shoring stage.
scenario: Vertical steel members are installed along the excavation perimeter before soil is removed between them.
visual: Excavation section showing vertical H-piles at intervals with retaining elements between them.
common_mistakes: A soldier pile is not the lagging itself.
Pile size, spacing, embedment, and installation method are engineered.

definition_en: Horizontal boards, panels, or structural elements installed between soldier piles to retain soil as excavation progresses.
explanation_ru: Lagging — горизонтальные доски, панели или иные элементы между soldier piles, которые удерживают грунт по мере углубления котлована.
example_en: Place the lagging progressively as the excavation is lowered.
scenario: Soil is removed in stages and retaining panels are inserted between previously installed vertical piles.
visual: Shoring elevation showing horizontal panels spanning between vertical soldier piles.
common_mistakes: Lagging retains soil between supports; it is not the main vertical pile.
Material and thickness depend on the engineered shoring design.

definition_en: A horizontal structural member that distributes shoring loads along a wall to tiebacks, struts, rakers, or other supports.
explanation_ru: Waler — горизонтальная балка вдоль shoring wall, которая собирает и распределяет боковую нагрузку между анкерами, struts/rakers и элементами ограждения.
translation_vi: dầm phân phối tải tường chắn
example_en: Install the waler at the anchor level before stressing the tiebacks.
scenario: A continuous horizontal beam links several shoring supports so wall loads are shared rather than concentrated at one point.
visual: Shoring wall with a horizontal beam connecting several support points.
common_mistakes: Do not confuse a waler with lagging; they have different structural roles.
Waler size and connection details come from the shoring design.

definition_en: An internal compression brace used to support opposite excavation walls or transfer shoring loads to another structural support.
explanation_ru: Strut — внутренняя распорка, работающая на сжатие. Её ставят внутри котлована, когда стенки shoring поддерживают друг друга или передают нагрузку на внутреннюю систему распорок.
example_en: Provide a strut where internal bracing is required instead of tieback anchors.
scenario: The excavation cannot use anchors beyond the property line, so compression braces span within the cut.
visual: Excavation section with a horizontal compression brace spanning between two shoring walls.
common_mistakes: A strut works mainly in compression and can obstruct access inside the excavation.
Do not assume tiebacks can be replaced by struts without redesign.

definition_en: An inclined compression brace used to support a shoring wall by transferring lateral load down to a footing, block, slab, or other reaction point.
explanation_ru: Raker — наклонная распорка шоринга. Она передаёт боковую нагрузку от стены вниз на опорный блок, footing или другое основание внутри котлована.
example_en: Use a raker where the shoring wall requires internal inclined bracing.
scenario: An excavation wall needs support but a horizontal brace would block the work area, so an inclined compression member is used.
visual: Shoring section with an inclined brace from the wall down to an interior reaction block.
common_mistakes: Rakers consume working space inside the excavation.
Reaction blocks and connections are engineered components, not incidental concrete.

definition_en: A continuous shoring wall formed by overlapping bored concrete piles, commonly used for deep excavations where stiffness and groundwater cutoff are important.
explanation_ru: Secant pile wall — сплошная стена из взаимно перекрывающихся буронабивных бетонных свай. Её применяют для глубоких котлованов, ограниченных площадок и там, где важен контроль грунта и воды.
example_en: Price the secant pile wall separately from conventional soldier-pile-and-lagging shoring.
scenario: Overlapping drilled piles create a nearly continuous retaining wall around a deep excavation.
visual: Plan and section showing overlapping circular piles forming a continuous perimeter wall.
common_mistakes: A secant pile wall is different from spaced soldier piles with lagging.
Pile overlap, reinforcement, tolerances, and water control are design-specific.

definition_en: Concrete or mortar pneumatically projected at high velocity onto a surface, often used for shoring facing, slope stabilization, repair, and structural work.
explanation_ru: Shotcrete — бетон/раствор, который наносят под давлением через сопло. На excavation проектах его часто используют как facing шоринга или для стабилизации поверхности грунта.
example_en: Apply shotcrete to the exposed shoring face where the design requires a continuous facing.
scenario: Fresh concrete is sprayed onto a vertical excavation support surface instead of being poured into conventional forms.
visual: Worker nozzle spraying concrete onto an excavation wall supported by reinforcement.
common_mistakes: Shotcrete placement is not the same as ordinary cast-in-place concrete.
Thickness, reinforcement, surface preparation, and testing follow the design/specification.

definition_en: Temporary or permanent work that strengthens or deepens an existing foundation so nearby excavation or new construction does not undermine it.
explanation_ru: Underpinning — усиление или углубление существующего фундамента. Может понадобиться, когда новый глубокий котлован подходит слишком близко к соседнему зданию или существующей foundation.
example_en: Include underpinning only where the temporary works or structural design requires support of the existing foundation.
scenario: A new basement extends below an adjacent existing footing, so the old foundation needs additional support before excavation continues.
visual: Section showing an existing shallow footing supported by new deeper underpinning elements beside an excavation.
common_mistakes: Underpinning is engineered temporary/structural work, not ordinary excavation.
Do not assume it is included in shoring unless the scope clearly says so.

definition_en: An additional load applied near an excavation or retaining system from buildings, traffic, stockpiles, cranes, equipment, or other sources above the retained ground.
explanation_ru: Surcharge load — дополнительная нагрузка у края котлована: здание, техника, traffic, stockpile, crane и т. п. Эта нагрузка увеличивает давление на shoring и влияет на temporary works design.
translation_vi: tải trọng phụ cạnh hố đào
example_en: Account for the surcharge load from construction equipment near the shoring wall.
scenario: Heavy equipment sits close to the excavation edge and adds lateral demand to the retaining system.
visual: Excavation section with equipment at grade and arrows showing added load toward the shoring wall.
common_mistakes: Surcharge is not limited to buildings; temporary construction loads also matter.
Keep heavy stockpiles and equipment locations consistent with the shoring design.

definition_en: The placement or injection of grout around a ground anchor or tieback to form the bonded zone that transfers anchor load into soil or rock.
explanation_ru: Anchor grouting — инъектирование grout вокруг tieback/ground anchor для создания bonded zone, через которую усилие анкера передаётся в грунт или скалу.
example_en: Carry anchor grouting as part of the tieback system when it is included in the shoring design.
scenario: After an anchor hole is drilled and the tendon is installed, grout is injected so the anchor can develop bond with the ground.
visual: Section showing an inclined tieback with a grouted bond zone behind the shoring wall.
common_mistakes: Grouting details and pressures are engineered and system-specific.
Do not treat optional post-grouting or regrouting as automatically included in the base anchor price.

definition_en: An isolated footing that supports a single column or concentrated load and spreads it into the soil over a wider base area.
explanation_ru: Pad footing — отдельный фундамент под колонну или другую сосредоточенную нагрузку. В excavation takeoff обычно считается отдельной rectangular/stepped выемкой.
example_en: Measure each pad footing separately where column foundations occur at different elevations.
scenario: Individual columns bear on separate widened concrete bases rather than one continuous strip.
visual: Plan and section showing an isolated square concrete footing beneath a column.
common_mistakes: Do not assume every isolated footing has the same depth or working-space requirement.
Pad footing and strip footing quantities should not be mixed.

definition_en: A reinforced concrete beam at or near ground level that spans between foundations or supports walls, while transferring loads to footings, piles, or other supports.
explanation_ru: Grade beam — железобетонная балка у уровня земли/ниже земли, которая соединяет foundations или несёт стены и передаёт нагрузку на footings/piles. Для excavation она часто требует длинной узкой выемки.
example_en: Excavate the grade beam trench after confirming its underside and adjacent footing elevations.
scenario: A continuous reinforced beam links separate foundation supports and carries a wall above.
visual: Section showing a reinforced beam spanning between two isolated foundations.
common_mistakes: A grade beam is structural concrete, not merely a thickened slab edge.
Check whether it bears on soil or spans between supports.

definition_en: A large continuous reinforced concrete foundation, also called a raft foundation, that supports many columns, walls, or a building core over a broad area.
explanation_ru: Mat foundation / raft foundation — большая сплошная железобетонная фундаментная плита, распределяющая нагрузку от многих колонн/стен по большой площади.
example_en: Treat the mat foundation as a large continuous foundation excavation rather than separate isolated footings.
scenario: Many structural loads are supported by one thick reinforced concrete foundation covering most of the building footprint.
visual: Section showing columns and core walls bearing on one thick continuous foundation slab.
common_mistakes: A mat foundation is much thicker and more heavily reinforced than a typical floor slab.
Raft foundation is a common synonym.

definition_en: A depressed structural pit below the lowest elevator landing that provides required space beneath the elevator car and equipment.
explanation_ru: Elevator pit — углубление ниже самого нижнего уровня лифта. Для estimator это отдельная глубокая excavation внутри core, обычно с более низкой bottom elevation, стенами и slab.
example_en: Measure the elevator pit excavation below the surrounding core foundation level.
scenario: The elevator shaft continues below the lowest floor into a deeper structural pocket.
visual: Core section showing an elevator shaft extending into a depressed pit below the lowest slab.
common_mistakes: Do not stop the excavation quantity at the lowest floor slab elevation.
Coordinate pit depth with structural and elevator drawings.

definition_en: A localized depressed pit that collects drainage or groundwater so it can be pumped to an approved discharge or drainage system.
explanation_ru: Sump pit — локальный приямок для сбора воды. В building excavation он может быть частью permanent drainage или временного dewatering и обычно требует отдельной глубокой выемки.
example_en: Excavate the sump pit to the required bottom elevation before installing the drainage components.
scenario: Water is directed to one low point below the surrounding floor so a pump can remove it.
visual: Section showing a depressed pit below slab level with water collection arrows.
common_mistakes: A permanent sump pit and a temporary excavation sump are not necessarily the same scope.
Check pump, piping, waterproofing, and discharge requirements separately.

definition_en: A concrete slab cast directly on prepared ground or granular base rather than spanning structurally between beams, walls, or columns.
explanation_ru: Slab on grade — бетонная плита по подготовленному грунту/гранулярному основанию. Под ней обычно координируются subgrade, slab prep и underground services.
translation_vi: sàn bê tông trên nền đất
example_en: Complete the underground services and slab preparation before placing the slab on grade.
scenario: A floor slab is supported continuously by prepared ground rather than suspended over open space.
visual: Cross-section showing concrete slab over granular base and compacted subgrade.
common_mistakes: Do not confuse slab on grade with a suspended structural slab.
Under-slab layers vary by project.

definition_en: A thin layer of low-strength concrete placed over soil or granular base to provide a clean, stable working surface for reinforcement, waterproofing, or foundation construction.
explanation_ru: Mud slab — тонкий слой слабого/lean concrete по грунту, создающий чистую ровную рабочую поверхность под foundation, waterproofing или rebar. Также может называться blinding concrete.
example_en: Place the mud slab over the trimmed excavation before foundation reinforcement work begins.
scenario: After excavation reaches grade, a thin non-structural concrete layer creates a clean base for the structural foundation work.
visual: Section showing a thin concrete layer beneath a thicker structural footing or mat foundation.
common_mistakes: A mud slab is generally not the main structural foundation.
Thickness and strength must come from the project requirements.

definition_en: The elevation at which a footing or foundation is intended to bear on competent supporting soil, rock, or engineered material.
explanation_ru: Bearing elevation — проектная отметка подошвы/опирания foundation. От неё зависит глубина footing excavation и проверка zone of influence рядом с глубокими services.
translation_vi: cao độ chịu tải của móng
example_en: Use the bearing elevation to calculate the footing excavation depth from the surrounding excavation level.
scenario: The structural detail identifies the level where the foundation must contact suitable supporting material.
visual: Foundation section with a labelled horizontal bearing line beneath the footing.
common_mistakes: Bearing elevation is not always the same as bottom of excavation if a mud slab or granular layer is below the footing.
Confirm whether drawings reference underside of concrete or prepared bearing surface.

definition_en: The elevation at the top of a manhole, catch basin, chamber, or similar structure where its cover or frame meets the finished surface.
explanation_ru: Rim elevation — отметка верха manhole/catch basin/chamber, обычно у cover/frame на finished grade. Вместе с invert или structure bottom помогает понять полную глубину.
example_en: Compare the rim elevation with the invert and structure bottom to check the chamber depth.
scenario: A utility structure has a top cover at finished grade and pipe connections lower inside it.
visual: Vertical structure section labelled at cover level and at lower pipe/invert elevations.
common_mistakes: Rim elevation is the top reference, not the pipe invert.
Always confirm whether the drawing uses rim, lid, frame, or finished-grade terminology.

definition_en: Excavation carried deeper or wider than the nominal design limit, either intentionally for unsuitable material removal, working space, replacement fill, or by construction tolerance.
explanation_ru: Over-excavation — дополнительная выемка сверх номинальной линии проекта по глубине или ширине. Может быть преднамеренной из-за плохого грунта или замены material, либо нежелательной.
example_en: Track over-excavation separately where unsuitable material must be removed below the planned subgrade.
scenario: The design cut is reached but weak material continues below it and must be removed before replacement fill is placed.
visual: Excavation section showing the design line and a deeper localized removal zone below it.
common_mistakes: Do not automatically include all over-excavation in the base quantity unless the scope requires it.
Replacement material and disposal can be separate costs.

definition_en: A temporary sloped access route built into or through an excavation so trucks and equipment can enter and exit lower working levels.
explanation_ru: Excavation ramp — временный съезд в котлован для excavators, loaders и trucks. Его объём и последующее removal могут влиять на production и последовательность bulk excavation.
example_en: Allow for the excavation ramp when planning truck access and the final bulk cut sequence.
scenario: Haul trucks must reach the bottom of a deep excavation, so part of the soil is temporarily left or built into a sloped access route.
visual: Deep excavation section with a sloping truck access route from grade to the bottom.
common_mistakes: Ramp material may be excavated later, so avoid double counting its volume.
Ramp grade and width depend on equipment, safety, and site constraints.

definition_en: A temporary pile of excavated soil, aggregate, backfill, or other bulk material stored on site for later reuse, loading, or disposal.
explanation_ru: Stockpile — временная куча/склад грунта или aggregate на площадке. В earthworks estimating влияет на rehandling, space, surcharge near shoring, moisture и haul logistics.
example_en: Keep the stockpile away from the excavation edge unless the shoring design allows the surcharge.
scenario: Excavated soil is kept on site for later reuse instead of being hauled away immediately.
visual: Site plan showing a material pile, equipment access, and setback from an excavation edge.
common_mistakes: Stockpiling can create rehandling cost and shoring surcharge.
Not all excavated material is suitable or permitted for reuse.

definition_en: Fill material brought onto the project from an off-site source because suitable on-site material is unavailable, insufficient, or not approved for reuse.
explanation_ru: Imported fill — материал обратной засыпки/насыпи, который завозят на площадку извне. В цене обычно важны material supply, trucking, placement и compaction.
translation_vi: đất đắp chở từ ngoài vào
example_en: Price imported fill separately when native excavated soil cannot satisfy the backfill requirements.
scenario: The project needs more suitable fill than can be reused from the excavation, so approved material is hauled in.
visual: Truck delivering aggregate/fill into a placement area beside an excavation.
common_mistakes: Imported fill cost is not only the material purchase price.
Verify source, gradation/specification, moisture, trucking, placement, and compaction.

definition_en: The fee charged by a disposal, transfer, recycling, or soil facility to accept a load of excavated material or construction debris.
explanation_ru: Tipping fee / dump fee — плата площадке приёмки за каждую нагрузку/тонну/объём вывезенного material. Это отдельный cost от самого trucking.
example_en: Include the tipping fee separately from truck time when pricing off-site disposal.
scenario: A haul truck reaches an approved facility and the estimator must account for the facility's charge to accept the load.
visual: Haul truck entering a disposal facility with a fee ticket symbol.
common_mistakes: Tipping fees can vary by material classification and facility.
Do not assume trucking includes disposal fees unless the quote clearly says so.

definition_en: The travel distance between the project and a material source, disposal site, or other destination used to estimate trucking time and cost.
explanation_ru: Haul distance — расстояние перевозки между площадкой и dump/source. Оно напрямую влияет на truck cycle time, количество trucks и production.
example_en: Check the haul distance before using historical trucking rates for soil export.
scenario: The same excavated volume can have very different transport cost depending on how far the truck must travel.
visual: Simple route diagram between construction site and disposal/source location with a distance arrow.
common_mistakes: Distance alone is not enough; traffic, queueing, and loading/unloading time also matter.
Use one-way or round-trip distance consistently.

definition_en: The total time for one truck to be loaded, travel to its destination, unload, return, and become available for the next load.
explanation_ru: Truck cycle time — полный цикл самосвала: loading → haul → dump → return → ready for next load. По нему estimator определяет нужное количество trucks под excavator production.
translation_vi: thời gian chu kỳ xe tải
example_en: Use truck cycle time to size the hauling fleet so the excavator is not waiting for trucks.
scenario: A truck repeats the same loading, travel, dumping, and return sequence throughout the shift.
visual: Circular flow diagram with load, haul, dump, return, and repeat.
common_mistakes: Too few trucks can idle the excavator; too many can create queues.
Cycle time changes with traffic, queueing, and site access.

definition_en: A factor describing the increase in volume that occurs when in-situ soil or rock is excavated and becomes loose material.
explanation_ru: Swell factor — увеличение объёма после выемки грунта. Bank volume после рыхления занимает больше loose volume, что важно для truck loads и disposal.
translation_vi: hệ số tăng thể tích sau đào
example_en: Apply the swell factor when converting bank excavation volume into estimated loose trucked volume.
scenario: Material occupies more space after excavation because the compact in-place structure is disturbed.
visual: Three-volume comparison showing smaller in-place block and larger loose pile after excavation.
common_mistakes: Do not use one swell factor for every soil or rock type.
Keep bank, loose, and compacted volume bases clearly labelled.

definition_en: A cubic metre of material measured in its natural undisturbed in-place condition before excavation.
explanation_ru: Bank cubic metre (BCM) — кубометр грунта в естественном положении до выемки. Это типичная база для earthwork takeoff; после excavation тот же material может иметь больший loose volume.
example_en: Report bulk excavation in bank cubic metre quantities unless the estimate clearly uses another volume basis.
scenario: The takeoff measures the volume of soil as it exists in the ground before the excavator loosens it.
visual: In-place soil block labelled before excavation, contrasted with a loose pile.
common_mistakes: BCM is a volume basis, not a soil classification.
Do not compare a bank quantity directly with loose truck capacity without conversion.

definition_en: A cubic metre of excavated material measured in a loose, uncompacted condition after it has been dug or handled.
explanation_ru: Loose cubic metre (LCM) — кубометр разрыхлённого грунта после excavation. Обычно нужен для truck capacity, stockpile и disposal calculations.
example_en: Convert the bank quantity to loose cubic metre volume when estimating truck loads.
scenario: Excavated soil forms a loose pile that occupies more space than it did in the ground.
visual: Loose soil pile labelled after excavation beside a smaller in-place reference block.
common_mistakes: LCM and BCM are not interchangeable.
Truck box volume normally relates more closely to loose material than bank quantity.

definition_en: Soil or other material that does not meet the required properties for the intended support, backfill, or embankment use and therefore may require removal, treatment, or replacement.
explanation_ru: Unsuitable material — грунт/материал, который нельзя оставить или использовать по назначению из-за слабости, органики, влажности, contamination или несоответствия specification.
example_en: Remove unsuitable material below subgrade and replace it with approved material where directed.
scenario: The planned subgrade is reached but the exposed soil cannot provide the required support.
visual: Subgrade section with a localized weak zone removed and replaced by approved fill.
common_mistakes: Unsuitable material is defined by the project/geotechnical requirements, not appearance alone.
Removal often creates both disposal and replacement-fill costs.

definition_en: A dewatering method that collects water in a low point or sump within the excavation and removes it with a pump.
explanation_ru: Sump pumping — простой способ dewatering: вода стекает в низкую точку/приямок, откуда её откачивают насосом. Подходит не для всех грунтов и глубин.
example_en: Use sump pumping for localized inflow only where the excavation and soil conditions permit it.
scenario: Seepage is directed to a low collection point and pumped out of the excavation.
visual: Excavation with water arrows flowing to a low sump and a pump discharge line.
common_mistakes: Sump pumping can draw fines or destabilize some soils.
Discharge treatment and location may be regulated or specified.

definition_en: A physical or clearance conflict between a proposed or existing utility and another pipe, structure, foundation, duct bank, or construction element.
explanation_ru: Utility conflict — пересечение/столкновение utility с другим pipe, footing, chamber, duct bank или structural element. На estimate/design review это часто требует lowering, rerouting, dropped footing или RFI.
translation_vi: xung đột hạ tầng kỹ thuật
example_en: Flag the utility conflict where the deep chamber enters the footing influence zone.
scenario: A proposed pipe or chamber occupies the same space needed by another structure or utility.
visual: Plan and section showing two proposed elements overlapping at one location.
common_mistakes: A utility crossing is not automatically a conflict if elevations provide clearance.
Resolve conflicts using all relevant plan/profile/structural information.

definition_en: Work required by the project that is not clearly included in any contractor or subcontractor scope, creating risk of an unpriced responsibility.
explanation_ru: Scope gap — работа нужна, но ни один proposal/scope явно её не включает. Типичный пример — неясно, кто демонтирует существующие below-grade элементы.
translation_vi: khoảng trống phạm vi công việc
example_en: Resolve the scope gap before bid close so required work is not omitted from the estimate.
scenario: Two trade proposals stop at different boundaries and a required piece of work falls between them.
visual: Scope diagram with two adjacent trade boxes and a highlighted uncovered gap between them.
common_mistakes: Scope gaps can exist even when every trade has submitted a quote.
Use clarifications or RFIs rather than silently assuming another party carries the work.

definition_en: A specific item, service, material, or responsibility explicitly included in a contractor's quoted scope and price.
explanation_ru: Inclusion — то, что proposal прямо включает в цену. При bid leveling важно сравнивать inclusions между subs, а не только totals.
translation_vi: nội dung đã tính trong giá
example_en: Confirm each inclusion before carrying a subcontractor quote in the estimate.
scenario: A proposal lists the work and services covered by the quoted price.
visual: Proposal page with a highlighted INCLUDED scope list.
common_mistakes: An inclusion can still have limits or qualifications.
Do not infer an inclusion only from the trade name.

definition_en: A specific item, service, material, or responsibility explicitly not included in a contractor's quoted scope or price.
explanation_ru: Exclusion — то, что sub прямо исключает из своей цены. Именно exclusions часто создают scope gaps или делают «самую низкую» quote фактически дороже.
example_en: Add or cover each exclusion before comparing the final leveled subcontractor prices.
scenario: A proposal identifies work that the bidder will not provide under the quoted price.
visual: Proposal page with a highlighted EXCLUDED scope list.
common_mistakes: An exclusion is not necessarily an error; it may belong to another trade.
Do not ignore small exclusions that carry large downstream cost.

definition_en: A condition, assumption, limitation, or clarification attached to a contractor's proposal that defines how its price or scope should be interpreted.
explanation_ru: Qualification — условие/оговорка в quote. Например цена действует при определённом access, hours, quantities, schedule или responsibility split.
translation_vi: ghi chú hạn chế phạm vi
example_en: Review every qualification before deciding whether two subcontractor prices are truly comparable.
scenario: A bidder's price is valid only under stated assumptions about access, schedule, quantities, or responsibilities.
visual: Proposal page with a highlighted CONDITIONS / QUALIFICATIONS section.
common_mistakes: Qualifications can materially change risk even when the quoted total looks low.
Carry important qualifications into the estimate notes and clarifications.

definition_en: The cost and activity of bringing crews, equipment, temporary facilities, and resources to the project and setting them up to begin work.
explanation_ru: Mobilization — доставка и первоначальная организация crews/equipment на проекте. Для shoring, excavation, cranes, pumps и specialty subs это часто отдельная заметная стоимость.
translation_vi: huy động thiết bị và nhân lực
example_en: Include mobilization separately when the subcontractor quote does not bury it in the unit rates.
scenario: Before production begins, equipment and crews must travel to site, unload, set up, and become ready to work.
visual: Equipment truck arriving at a jobsite with setup arrows toward the work area.
common_mistakes: Mobilization is not production quantity itself.
Multiple phases or remobilizations can create more than one mobilization cost.

definition_en: Paid or cost-incurring time when labor or equipment is available at or for the project but cannot perform productive work because of delay, access, coordination, inspection, breakdown, or another constraint.
explanation_ru: Standby time — оплачиваемое/затратное ожидание, когда crew или equipment готовы, но не могут работать из-за задержки, доступа, coordination и т. п.
example_en: Check the standby time terms for pumps, trucks, cranes, and specialty equipment before using the quoted rate.
scenario: Equipment remains on site and incurs cost while another activity prevents productive work.
visual: Machine parked beside an active work zone with a clock symbol.
common_mistakes: Standby rules differ by supplier and subcontractor.
Separate avoidable idle time from contractual standby charges.

definition_en: Past project, bid, purchase, or subcontract pricing used as a reference when developing or checking a current estimate.
explanation_ru: Historical pricing — прошлые цены с похожих проектов, которые используют как benchmark. Их нужно нормализовать по date, scope, quantity, location и market conditions, а не копировать вслепую.
translation_vi: dữ liệu giá từ dự án trước
example_en: Use historical pricing from similar excavation projects as a reference, then adjust it for current scope and timing.
scenario: The estimator reviews recent comparable jobs to test whether a new budget rate is reasonable.
visual: Comparison sheet showing prior project rates adjusted to a current estimate date.
common_mistakes: Past pricing is a reference, not automatically today's market price.
Check scope, date, quantity, location, and escalation before reuse.

definition_en: An allowance or forecast for future increases in labor, material, equipment, subcontract, or other costs between the estimate date and the time the work will be performed.
explanation_ru: Escalation — ожидаемый рост стоимости между сегодняшним estimate и будущим construction. Для phase, которая будет строиться через годы, нельзя просто считать сегодняшнюю firm quote вечной.
translation_vi: tăng chi phí theo thời gian
example_en: Apply an escalation assumption to the future phase when the work will occur well after the current estimate date.
scenario: A budget prepared today must account for the possibility that construction costs will be higher in a later year.
visual: Timeline from estimate date to construction date with an upward cost arrow.
common_mistakes: Escalation is time-related cost growth, not the same as contingency for unknown scope.
State the base date, future date, and escalation assumption.

definition_en: The period during which a quoted price remains open and can be accepted without the bidder requiring repricing.
explanation_ru: Price validity — срок действия quote. Особенно важно, если construction далеко в будущем: sub может дать цену valid 30/60/90 days, но не до далёкой future phase.
translation_vi: thời hạn hiệu lực báo giá
example_en: Record the price validity when using a subcontractor quote for a future construction phase.
scenario: A bidder states that its quoted price can be accepted only until a specified date.
visual: Proposal header with quote date, expiry date, and a highlighted validity window.
common_mistakes: Expired pricing may still be useful as a benchmark but is not a firm current commitment.
Do not confuse quote validity with the project construction schedule.

definition_en: A cast-in-place or precast concrete curb with a rounded exposed top or face profile, shaped according to a project, municipal, or owner standard detail.
explanation_ru: Bullnose curb — бетонный бордюр с округлённым верхом или лицевой гранью. Точная геометрия зависит от стандартного detail проекта/муниципалитета. В смете важно не путать его с обычным barrier curb или curb and gutter: могут отличаться форма, опалубка, армирование, способ оплаты и производительность.
translation_vi: bó vỉa bê tông bo tròn
example_en: Price the bullnose curb separately where the drawings call for the rounded curb profile.
scenario: A concrete restoration detail shows a rounded curb profile rather than a standard vertical curb face.
visual: Cross-section comparing a rounded bullnose concrete curb profile with adjacent pavement and sidewalk.
common_mistakes: Bullnose curb dimensions are not universal; always use the project or municipal standard detail.
Do not assume a bullnose curb is the same as curb and gutter or mountable curb simply because the exposed face is rounded.

definition_en: A raised concrete curb with a relatively steep or near-vertical traffic-side face intended to discourage vehicles from crossing it and to define the roadway edge.
explanation_ru: Barrier curb — высокий бетонный бордюр с почти вертикальной дорожной гранью. Он физически отделяет проезжую часть и не предназначен для обычного переезда автомобилем. Профиль и размеры берут из стандартного detail.
example_en: Restore the barrier curb to the same profile and elevation as the existing curb.
scenario: A roadway edge needs a raised curb that clearly separates vehicle traffic from the boulevard or sidewalk.
visual: Road cross-section with asphalt meeting a raised concrete curb with a steep traffic-side face.
common_mistakes: Barrier curb is generally less traversable than mountable curb; verify the actual standard section instead of judging only by the name.

definition_en: A concrete curb with a sloped or low rounded face designed so vehicles can cross it more easily than a barrier curb where permitted.
explanation_ru: Mountable curb — переезжаемый бордюр с пологой или низкой округлой гранью. Машина может пересечь его легче, чем barrier curb. Часто встречается у жилых дорог, парковок и некоторых driveway transitions.
translation_vi: bó vỉa có thể chạy qua
example_en: Replace the damaged mountable curb along the driveway frontage.
scenario: A curb profile is intentionally sloped so vehicle tires can pass over it without a vertical curb face.
visual: Cross-section showing pavement meeting a low sloped concrete curb that a vehicle tire can cross.
common_mistakes: Mountable curb does not mean every vehicle crossing is automatically acceptable; geometry and permitted use depend on the design.

definition_en: The curved section of curb that transitions around a street corner, driveway, island, or other change in roadway edge alignment.
explanation_ru: Curb return — криволинейный участок бордюра, который поворачивает линию curb вокруг угла перекрёстка, driveway, островка или другого изменения направления. В takeoff его длину обычно измеряют по кривой, а не по хорде.
example_en: Measure the curb return along the arc rather than using the straight chord length.
scenario: At an intersection corner the curb line bends through a radius instead of continuing straight.
visual: Plan view showing two straight curb lines connected by a curved radius at a corner.
common_mistakes: For quantity takeoff, a curb return is measured along its actual curved length unless the bid documents state otherwise.

definition_en: A sloped pedestrian transition between a sidewalk and roadway that lowers or removes the curb barrier at a crossing, usually designed to accessibility requirements.
explanation_ru: Curb ramp — пониженный наклонный участок тротуара/бордюра для перехода между sidewalk и roadway. Обычно выполняется по требованиям accessibility и может включать detectable warning surface.
translation_vi: ram dốc cho người đi bộ
example_en: Reconstruct the curb ramp to the accessibility detail after the utility crossing.
scenario: A sidewalk crossing needs a gradual sloped transition down to roadway elevation rather than a vertical curb.
visual: Plan and section showing sidewalk sloping down through a curb ramp to roadway level with a detectable warning zone.
common_mistakes: Do not treat a curb ramp as ordinary flat sidewalk; slopes, landings, widths, and detectable warning requirements are detail-specific.

definition_en: A concrete vehicular access slab connecting a roadway or lane to a property, parking area, garage, or site entrance.
explanation_ru: Concrete driveway — бетонный автомобильный въезд. В restoration estimate нужно проверить толщину slab, base preparation, reinforcement if required, joints, limits to nearest panel/joint, curb transition и tie-in к существующему покрытию.
translation_vi: lối xe vào bằng bê tông
example_en: Restore the 200 mm concrete driveway after the utility trench is backfilled and compacted.
scenario: A utility crossing cuts through a concrete vehicle entrance and the affected driveway panel must be reconstructed.
visual: Plan and section of a concrete driveway slab crossing the boulevard between roadway curb and private property.
common_mistakes: Do not assume driveway thickness matches sidewalk thickness; use the project or municipal detail.
Restoration limits may extend to full panels or joints rather than only the trench width.

definition_en: The concrete drainage strip or channel immediately adjacent to a curb that collects roadway runoff and directs it toward catch basins or other drainage inlets.
explanation_ru: Gutter pan — бетонная водоотводная полоса/лоток непосредственно у бордюра. В monolithic curb and gutter она является нижней дорожной частью профиля, по которой вода идёт к catch basin.
translation_vi: máng thoát nước cạnh bó vỉa
rãnh bê tông sát bó vỉa
example_en: Match the gutter pan grade so runoff continues to drain toward the catch basin.
scenario: Rainwater flows along the low concrete strip beside the curb before entering a drainage inlet.
visual: Road cross-section showing curb face and adjacent sloped concrete gutter pan carrying runoff.
common_mistakes: Gutter pan is the drainage portion beside the curb; it is not the same thing as the raised curb face.
